title: LanguageSpec
description: Spec for a generated programming language. Stage 1 produces a base spec with some auto/null fields; the resolver fills them in.

loop_forms.description: Family-specific iteration constructs the language supports. c_like and python_like: pick from ['while', 'c_for', 'foreach', 'repeat_until', 'loop_break'] as appropriate. s_expression: typically ['while'] (lisplang has a while special form). stack_based: ['begin', 'until', 'do', 'loop'] are stack-based families' loop words (but those aren't in this enum since they're family-specific words, not generic forms - typically the spec just lists ['while'] here). ml_like: MUST be the empty array `[]`. mllang has NO while/for loops; iteration is recursion + pattern matching on list cons. Do NOT add 'while' to an ml_like spec's loop_forms - the grammar does not parse it and downstream stages will fail.

comment_syntax.description: Family-specific comment syntax. Preserve the value present in the base spec for the language's syntax family; do not rewrite to a different family's comment markers. c_like: line '//', block '/* */'. python_like: line '#', no block. s_expression: line ';', no block. stack_based: line '\', block '( )'. ml_like: line null (no line comments), block '(* *)' (nestable in real OCaml; v1 treats outermost pair only).

line.description: Single-line comment marker. Family-specific values: c_like '//', python_like '#', s_expression ';', stack_based '\\' (backslash, escaped here), ml_like null (no line comments). Preserve the family's value from the base spec; do NOT default to '//' or '#'.

block_open.description: Opening token for block comments. Family-specific values: c_like '/*', python_like null (Python has no block comments; only line comments + triple-quoted strings), s_expression null (lisplang has no block comments), stack_based '(' (parens are paren-comments in Forth), ml_like '(*'. Preserve the family's value; do NOT default to '/*' or '"""' (the resolver historically wrote triple quotes for ml_like, which is wrong).

block_close.description: Closing token for block comments. Family-specific values: c_like '*/', python_like null, s_expression null, stack_based ')', ml_like '*)'. Must pair with block_open from the same family. Preserve the family's value; do NOT default.

nestable.description: Whether block comments can nest inside each other. Family defaults: c_like false (standard C/C++ rule), python_like false (no block comments anyway), s_expression false, stack_based false (Forth paren-comments don't nest in the standard), ml_like true (real OCaml nests; mllang v1 grammar treats outermost pair only but the source-level convention says nestable). Preserve the family's value from the base spec.

statement_terminator.description: Family-specific. c_like: ';'. python_like: 'newline'. s_expression: ')'. stack_based: ' ' (whitespace). ml_like: ';;'. Preserve the family-correct value from the base spec; do not rewrite to a different family's form.

block_style.description: Family-specific. c_like: 'braces'. python_like: 'indent'. s_expression: 'parens'. stack_based: 'concatenative'. ml_like: 'expression-oriented' (let-in chains, match, no blocks). Preserve the family-correct value from the base spec.

type_annotations.description: Required when typing=static, ignored when dynamic.

print_form.description: How to print to stdout, as a template containing '<args>' as the placeholder for the value being printed. Family-specific: c_like 'print(<args>);', python_like 'print(<args>)', s_expression '(print <args>)', stack_based '<args> .', ml_like 'print_any (<args>) ;;'. The resolver MUST preserve the value present in the base spec for the language's syntax family — do not rewrite to a different family's print form. Phrasebooks may override with their own template (e.g. 'say <args>').

type_system.description: Filled in by resolver when typing=static.

memory_model.description: Filled in by resolver. Documents the chosen semantics honestly.

stdlib.description: Stdlib functions exposed to user programs.

design_notes.description: Resolver-authored explanations for non-trivial design choices.

error_handling.description: Error-handling strategy. Family defaults: c_like 'panic_only' (or 'exceptions' if explicit), python_like 'exceptions', s_expression 'panic_only', stack_based 'panic_only', ml_like 'panic_only' (v1 has no exception system; unmatched `match` arms raise _MLMatchError at runtime).

loop_forms.description: Family-specific iteration constructs. Preserve what's appropriate for the syntax family. c_like and python_like: 'while', 'c_for', 'foreach' available. s_expression: typically 'while' or recursion-only. stack_based: 'begin/until', 'do/loop'. ml_like: empty array - mllang has NO while/for loops; iteration is recursion + pattern matching on list cons. The kata pack will use recursion for ml_like. Do NOT add 'while' to an ml_like spec's loop_forms - the grammar does not parse it.

customization.description: User-supplied overrides and additions. Survives the resolver round-trip.

extra_prompt_notes.description: Per-component free-form instructions appended to that component's prompt. Keys are component names.

additional_tests.description: User-supplied test pairs the verifier will require alongside the canonical 8.

natural_language.description: User-defined phrasebook. Each entry is a sentence template with <placeholder> slots; the parser uses these literal strings instead of the default keywords. Unspecified entries fall back to the language's default syntax.

origin_story.description: In-world 2-3 sentence description of where this language came from (roadmap §5.2 lore framing). Resolver fills this in.

lineage.description: Crossbreeding genealogy (roadmap §3.2 + §3.3). Present only for languages bred from existing parents.

parents.description: Names of the parent languages this child was crossed from.

strategy.description: Conflict-resolution strategy used at merge time.

generation.description: 1 = first-generation crossbreed; 2 = bred from a 1st-gen, etc.

seed.description: RNG seed (when 'random' strategy was used) so the merge is reproducible.
